label: Religious Traditionalism (classical Christian theism)
summary: The trinitarian theism of the Nicene Creed elaborated by Augustine, Anselm, and Aquinas: one transcendent, perfect, personal God created and providentially governs the world and has revealed himself in Scripture and in Christ. Humans are made in God's image, fallen, and offered redemption; history moves toward a divinely appointed consummation. Taken here as the concrete instance of the general religious-traditionalist pattern (revealed truth, sacred tradition, transcendent moral order) shared with orthodox Judaism, Islam, and traditionalist Hinduism.
variants: Catholic / Eastern Orthodox / Protestant (confessional vs evangelical vs liberal); classical theism vs open/process theism; young-earth creationism vs theistic evolution; Augustinian/Calvinist vs Thomist vs Arminian views of free will and providence. The same axis signature recurs in other scriptural traditionalisms with different revelation sources.

positions.summary: Justificationist: truth is grounded in divine revelation received through Scripture and tradition, harmonized with reason ('faith seeking understanding'). Fallibilism applies to humans, not to revelation itself.
Real knowledge is possible but bounded by mystery: finite minds cannot comprehend God's essence or providence fully.
Revelation, tradition, and magisterium (or sola scriptura) rank above unaided reason as sources of truth.
Strongly realist about objective truth — grounded in God's nature rather than in autonomous science.
Qualified: real goods from human creativity under the cultural mandate, but no salvation through material progress; ultimate hope is eschatological, and Babel-like hubris is a standing warning.
Prudence as cardinal virtue; suspicion of technologies that usurp the Creator's prerogatives (bioethics, transhumanism); stewardship rather than mastery.
Free will affirmed, variously reconciled with providence and predestination; agency is exercised within a divinely ordered structure.
Humans bear the image of God — of unique significance in creation, though creaturely and dependent rather than self-made.
Strongly objective morality grounded in God's nature, known via natural law and revealed commandments; sin is an objective condition.
Supernaturalist: God transcends nature; miracles are possible; humans have immortal souls; reality is created and purpose-laden.
Sacred tradition is a deposit to be guarded and handed on; doctrinal and moral continuity outrank innovation.
Stewardship: creation is good and entrusted to humans, to be cultivated but not exploited or wholly remade.
Meaning is given: to know, love, and glorify God and enjoy him forever — communion with God as humanity's telos.
Communal: the church, family, and covenant community are constitutive, though each soul is individually responsible before God.
